plan.title: Adipose treated vs control: variance partition + DE
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq gene-level count matrix from Salmon (12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples, counts.csv) with a 12 x 4 sample table (metadata.csv) recording condition (treated vs control, 6 vs 6), sex (F/M) and age (years) in human adipose tissue. The question has two parts in a fixed order: first how much of the per-gene expression variance condition, sex and age each explain, then which genes differ between treated and control.

T1S1 establishes the sample structure before any model: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap and library sizes, coloured by condition and by sex. With only 12 samples this is the step that catches an outlier or a sex-driven primary axis that would otherwise be read as a treatment effect. Single batch is declared, so there is no batch term to check.

T1S2 answers the first half of the question directly with variancePartition on voom log-CPM with precision weights: condition and sex as random effects (categorical), age centred as a fixed effect (continuous), giving the fraction of each gene's variance attributed to each term plus the residual. This is a design diagnostic, not a test — it is reported as a distribution across genes with medians per term, and it explicitly does not license dropping a term from the DE design.

T1S3 answers the second half. Minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, design ~ sex + age_centered + condition with control set as the explicit reference level, DESeq2 Wald test on the contrast condition treated vs control, apeglm shrinkage on the condition coefficient, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. Sex and age enter the design as fixed-effect terms rather than being regressed out of the counts. With 6 per group DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers to NA rather than replacing them, so NA causes are reported separately.

T1S4 is the robustness and reporting step: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and the same design, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap as the high-confidence set, MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram, and the full reproducibility record. n=6 per group is a small study; the report must state the number of tested genes and DE genes rather than lead with a gene story.

No enrichment step is planned — the research question asks for variance decomposition and a gene-level contrast only.
